name: Fernando Torres
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Atlético Madrid's senior team at 17 in May 2001 and won the UEFA European Under-16 Championship with Spain the same year; by 26 he was a Liverpool star, Euro 2008 winner, and Ballon d'Or third-place finisher.
early_history_summary: Torres joined Atlético Madrid's youth system at age 11 in 1995, signed his first professional contract at 15, and made his senior debut on 27 May 2001 at age 17. He was voted best player in Europe for his age group at the Nike Cup in 1998 and was named Atlético captain at 19. He joined Liverpool in 2007 and became one of the world's top strikers, finishing third for the Ballon d'Or in 2008 at age 24.
family_context_summary: Born in Fuenlabrada, Madrid; grandfather was an Atlético Madrid fan who influenced his passion. Family background beyond this is not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite youth academy, early specialization, physical talent, Spanish football golden era
evidence_summary: Torres progressed through Atlético Madrid's youth academy from age 11, was voted best player in Europe for his age group at 14, signed a professional contract at 15, and debuted for the senior team at 17. The Atlético Madrid youth pipeline and Spanish football ecosystem provided elite-level training and competition from a young age. His physical talent and goalscoring ability were evident early, earning him the nickname 'El Niño.' No family financial or domain advantage is documented.
starting_point: Born in Fuenlabrada, a working-class suburb of Madrid; grandfather was an Atlético Madrid fan who ignited his passion for the club. Family financial background not documented.
current_position: Manager of Atlético Madrid B; retired from professional football in 2019; estimated net worth ~$90M; resides in Spain.

name: Adolfo Pérez Esquivel
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Pérez Esquivel was teaching art and architecture in his twenties; his human rights activism began in the 1960s (age ~30), and he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1980 at age 49.
early_history_summary: Born to a Spanish immigrant fisherman in Buenos Aires, Pérez Esquivel's mother died when he was three. He began working with Christian pacifist groups in the 1960s and co-founded SERPAJ in 1974, leading to his Nobel Peace Prize in 1980.
family_context_summary: Born to a Spanish fisherman from Galicia who emigrated to Argentina; mother died when he was three. Grew up in poverty.

name: Arpad Sterbik
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal at the 1999 World Handball Championship with Yugoslavia at age 20; by 26 he was Hungarian league champion (2002-2004), Hungarian Handballer of the Year (2002), and IHF World Player of the Year (2005).
early_history_summary: Sterbik grew up in Senta, Serbia (then Yugoslavia) as an ethnic Hungarian. His father took him to handball training as a child. He began his career at RK Jugović and was called up to the Yugoslav national team at 19, debuting at the 1999 World Championship in Egypt where he won bronze. He moved to Fotex Veszprém in Hungary in 2001, winning three Hungarian league and cup titles and being named Hungarian Handballer of the Year in 2002.
family_context_summary: Born in Senta, Serbia (then Yugoslavia) as an ethnic Hungarian; father took him to handball training from a young age. Sister Andrea is also a professional handballer.

evidence_summary: Sterbik's 2.00m frame gave him an unusual physical edge as a goalkeeper. His father introduced him to handball early, and coach Zoran Tuta Zivkovic trusted him as a 19-year-old debutant at the 1999 World Championship. He won bronze there and moved to Hungarian top club Veszprém at 21, where he won multiple titles and was named Hungarian Handballer of the Year at 23. His sister is also a professional handballer, indicating a family-domain connection.

name: Iggy Pop
milestone_by_age_26: Released The Stooges' self-titled debut album on Elektra Records in August 1969 at age 22, followed by Fun House (1970) and Raw Power (1973), all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born James Newell Osterberg Jr. in a trailer park in Ypsilanti, Michigan, he began playing drums in the fifth grade. His parents gave up their master bedroom for his drum kit. He played in high school bands including the Iguanas, then joined the Prime Movers at 18. He dropped out of the University of Michigan, moved to Chicago to study blues, and formed the Psychedelic Stooges (later The Stooges) in 1967. The band signed with Elektra Records in 1968 and released their debut album produced by John Cale in 1969.
family_context_summary: Born in a trailer park in Ypsilanti, Michigan; father was an English teacher and baseball coach at Fordson High School in Dearborn. Parents were deeply supportive, giving up their master bedroom for his drum kit.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an English teacher and baseball coach; no music industry connection, but parents invested heavily in supporting his musical interests.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Detroit/Ann Arbor music scene, Stooges band formation, Elektra Records signing, counterculture wave, supportive parents
evidence_summary: Iggy Pop grew up in a trailer park but had profoundly supportive parents who gave up their bedroom for his drum kit. The Ann Arbor/Detroit music scene of the late 1960s, including proximity to MC5, provided a frontier ecosystem. The Stooges—formed with Ron and Scott Asheton and Dave Alexander—were a high-trust peer team that created a landmark proto-punk sound. Elektra Records signed them in 1968, and their debut album was released in 1969 when Pop was 22.
starting_point: Born in a trailer park in Ypsilanti, Michigan; father was an English teacher and baseball coach, mother of Danish-Norwegian descent; parents were supportive despite modest means, giving up their bedroom for his drum kit.
current_position: Active touring musician and cultural icon; regarded as the 'Godfather of Punk'; received Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2020; inducted into Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2010; continues performing as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Released The Stooges' self-titled debut album on Elektra Records, produced by John Cale.

Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of the Stooges.
Received the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award for his solo career.

name: Marian Cozma
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Romanian national championship with HC Dinamo București in the 2004-05 season at age 22-23; later won the Hungarian championship and EHF Cup Winners' Cup with KC Veszprém in 2008 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Cozma was born in Bucharest and guided into handball by his father Petre, a former handball player. He joined HC Dinamo București and played in the first squad from 2002 to 2006, winning the Romanian championship in 2004-05. He transferred to KC Veszprém in Hungary in 2006, where he won the Hungarian championship and EHF Cup Winners' Cup in 2008. He earned 60 caps for Romania before his tragic death in February 2009 at age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Tei, Bucharest; father Petre was a handball player who guided his son into the sport. Family financial background not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Petre was a former handball player who directly introduced and guided Marian into the sport from a young age.

evidence_summary: Cozma's father, a former handball player, guided him into the sport from a young age, providing direct domain apprenticeship. His exceptional 2.11m height gave him a significant physical edge as a pivot player. He progressed through HC Dinamo București, a top Romanian club, and won the national championship at 22-23. He also survived a stabbing attack by rival fans near his spine and returned to play, showing resilience. His career was cut short by his murder at age 26 in Hungary.

name: Mats Näslund
milestone_by_age_26: Won a bronze medal at the 1979 World Ice Hockey Championship with Sweden at age 20; by 26 he was an NHL All-Rookie Team selection (1983) and scored 110 points in the 1985-86 season, winning the Stanley Cup with Montreal at age 26.
early_history_summary: Näslund began his playing career with Timrå IK in Sweden's elite league at age 16 in 1975. He moved to Brynäs IF in 1978 and was drafted 37th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 1979 NHL Entry Draft. He won World Championship bronze with Sweden in 1979 and silver in 1981. He joined the Canadiens for the 1982-83 season, becoming the first European-born player to play for Montreal, and was named to the NHL All-Rookie Team with 71 points in 74 games.
family_context_summary: Born in Timrå, Sweden; family and financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish Elite League, Brynäs IF, Montreal Canadiens draft, European NHL pioneer, overcame small stature
evidence_summary: Näslund benefited from Sweden's elite hockey development pipeline, playing in the Swedish Elite League from age 16 and for Brynäs IF, a top club. He was drafted by the Montreal Canadiens at 20 and became the first European to play for the franchise. His small stature (5 feet 7 inches) was an adversity he overcame through skill and speed. No family background or financial advantage is documented.

current_position: Retired former NHL player; member of the IIHF Hall of Fame (inducted 2005); member of the Triple Gold Club; resides in Sweden.

name: Peter Nguyen Van Hung
category: Catholic priest and human rights activist
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. By 26 (1984), Nguyen Van Hung was in Japan working various labor jobs after fleeing Vietnam as a boat person in 1979; he was ordained as a priest in 1991 at age 33 and began his human rights work in Taiwan in 2004.
early_history_summary: Born into a lower-middle-class family in South Vietnam, Peter Nguyen Van Hung's father died after a long illness, forcing his mother to become the breadwinner. He fled Vietnam by boat in 1979 at age 21, was rescued by a Norwegian ship, and taken to Japan. He lived in Japan for three years studying and working as a highway repairman, steel factory worker, and gravedigger. He joined the Missionary Society of St. Columban, came to Taiwan as a missionary in 1988, and was ordained in 1991 in Australia.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a lower-middle-class family outside Bình Tuy Province in South Vietnam with two brothers and five sisters; father was a fisherman who died after long illness; mother became the family breadwinner.
evidence_summary: Nguyen Van Hung grew up in poverty in South Vietnam, losing his father to illness. He fled as a boat person at 21 and spent years in Japan doing manual labor before joining a missionary society. His ordination came at 33 and his notable human rights work began at 46. No material milestone by age 26 was identified.

She won Miss South Carolina Teen USA and then Miss Teen USA in 1998 at age 18, also winning Miss Congeniality.

name: Howie Mandel
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Mandel was a working comedian by his early twenties—performing at Yuk Yuk's in Toronto and The Comedy Store in LA, and appearing on Make Me Laugh (1979-80)—but his breakthrough came with a six-year run on St. Elsewhere starting in 1982 at age 27.
early_history_summary: Born in Toronto, Mandel was expelled from high school and worked as a carpet salesman. He began performing stand-up at Yuk Yuk's in Toronto, getting a week-long booking by September 1978 at age 22. On a trip to LA, he performed at The Comedy Store and became a regular, leading to appearances on Make Me Laugh (1979-80) and opening for David Letterman in 1979. His national breakthrough came with the NBC medical drama St. Elsewhere, which began in 1982 when he was 27.
family_context_summary: Born in Toronto; grew up in the Bathurst Manor neighborhood. Father was a lighting manufacturer and real estate magnate. Ancestors were Romanian and Polish Jews. Distant cousin of violinist Itzhak Perlman.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a lighting manufacturer and real estate magnate, no entertainment industry connection documented.
